C-CI-TOOLS-TIMEOUT.Name: Heavy tool-suite test timeouts raised
C-CI-TOOLS-TIMEOUT.Summary: The tests/tools spawn-fixture suites (run-rust-tests, qa-launch-gate, qa-artifact-smoke) drive real child processes through shims; under a loaded shared Windows runner their honest runs exceed the 5 s vitest default and surface as order-dependent timeout flakes across unrelated PRs. Each file gains vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30000 }) — the same containment already proven in tests/tools/dev-smoke.test.mjs.
C-CI-TOOLS-TIMEOUT.Problem: Three tool suites timed out at the 5 s default on windows-latest CI runners across PRs (#302/#303/#307/#310 evidence), forcing rerun churn on changes that never touch them.

Goals.Goal: Each named suite declares a 30 s per-test budget; no assertion or fixture changes.
The rust-test artifact cleanup tolerates the Windows EBUSY/EPERM unlink window with a bounded retry (av-scanner lock on just-reaped executables) — the same Windows-flake family.

C-CI-TOOLS-TIMEOUT.NonGoals: Any fixture, assertion or behavior change; global vitest config edits.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Each of the three files contains vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30000 }) after its vitest import; the three suites pass locally; grace lint final is clean.

C-CI-TOOLS-TIMEOUT.VerificationIntent: The three suites via npx vitest run; grace lint final --run-commands.
